title: Varun Dhawan Just Confirmed He Turned Down Andhadhun. The Original Cast Was Him and Kangana.
excerpt: In a conversation with Tanmay Bhat, the actor revealed that Sriram Raghavan built one of Bollywood's greatest thrillers around him — and he walked away because his calendar was full. The internet is now imagining the film that never was.
body:
Here's the thing about Bollywood's greatest what-ifs: they usually come out decades later, vague and deniable, buried in a memoir nobody reads. **Varun Dhawan** just dropped his on a YouTube show like it was nothing.

During a recent episode on **Tanmay Bhat's** channel, Varun was asked the question every actor dreads and every interviewer lives for: *What's the best film you said no to?*

His answer was immediate. No hedging, no diplomatic non-answer.

> "Andhadhun. I was filming for something else. So I couldn't do it. And the original cast of the film was supposed to be me and Kangana."

Let that land for a second. **Andhadhun** — the Sriram Raghavan black comedy thriller that went on to gross ₹456 crore worldwide, win multiple National Awards, and become arguably the most rewatched Hindi film of the last decade — was built around Varun Dhawan and **Kangana Ranaut**.

Not Ayushmann Khurrana. Not Tabu. Not Radhika Apte. The film that made Ayushmann an untouchable leading man, that gave Tabu the most deliciously wicked role of her career, that turned an indie-scaled thriller into a global phenomenon — it was supposed to be a completely different movie.

## The Badlapur Connection

The casting makes more sense than it initially sounds. Varun and Sriram Raghavan had already worked together on **Badlapur** in 2015 — a film that remains, eight years later, the darkest and most interesting thing Varun has ever done. It was the project that proved he could do more than dance and dimple his way through romantic comedies.

Raghavan clearly saw something in Varun that the industry's box office machinery kept trying to sand down. After *Badlapur*, the director started developing what would become *Andhadhun* with Varun in mind. The blind pianist who fakes his disability. The moral ambiguity. The darkness dressed up as farce.

But Varun's calendar was stacked. He was deep into other shooting commitments — likely the commercially driven projects that defined his mid-career — and the dates couldn't align. Raghavan, not one to wait around, moved on.

## The Kangana Question

Varun's mention of Kangana Ranaut as the original female lead adds another layer. If the original casting held, Kangana would have played one of the roles that ultimately went to either Tabu or Radhika Apte. Given her intensity and Raghavan's taste for morally complex women, the smart money says she was being considered for the Simi role — the character Tabu turned into one of Hindi cinema's all-time great villains.

Kangana has not commented on the revelation. She rarely does when someone else's interview becomes about her. But the casting hypothetical is irresistible: Varun's restrained physicality against Kangana's feral energy, directed by a filmmaker who loves to let actors unsettle each other.

Would it have worked? Maybe. Would it have been the same film? Absolutely not. And that's the point.

## What Actually Happened

**Ayushmann Khurrana** stepped into the role and made it inseparable from his identity. His Akash — the pianist who may or may not be blind, who may or may not be innocent — was so precisely calibrated that it's now impossible to imagine anyone else in the frame. Tabu's Simi became a masterclass in controlled menace. Radhika Apte brought warmth and credibility to a role that could have been a footnote.

The film opened modestly in October 2018, earned ₹74 crore in India, then exploded internationally — particularly in China, where it grossed over ₹300 crore and became one of the highest-earning Indian films in that market. It swept the National Awards. It's streaming on **JioHotstar** and **Amazon Prime Video** for anyone who needs a reminder of what it felt like to watch it for the first time.

## The Career Road Not Taken

Varun's admission carries a specific kind of sting. His career since *Badlapur* has been a tug-of-war between the commercial machine (the *Judwaa 2*s, the *Coolie No. 1* remake) and the occasional reach for something weightier (*October*, *Bhediya*). If *Andhadhun* had happened, the conversation around Varun Dhawan as an actor — not a star, an *actor* — would be fundamentally different.

Instead, that conversation belongs to Ayushmann. And Varun knows it. The fact that he said the quiet part out loud, on camera, without bitterness or excuse-making, is its own kind of maturity. He's currently promoting **Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai**, his father David Dhawan's latest — and reportedly final — directorial effort, which hit theatres last week.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZPLzYlDPPp/

Sometimes the most interesting version of a film is the one that never got made. Varun and Kangana in *Andhadhun* will live forever in the parallel universe where scheduling wasn't a problem and Bollywood's most explosive actress played a woman who buries bodies with a smile.

The rest of us got the version with Ayushmann and Tabu. We did just fine.
